title: A presheaf of abelian groups or commutative rings is a sheaf iff its underlying presheaf of sets is
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site (Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH) and let $\mathcal A$ be the category of abelian groups or the category of commutative rings, with forgetful functor $s:\mathcal A\to\textit{Sets}$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal C$ with values in $\mathcal A$, i.e. a functor $\mathcal C^{op}\to\mathcal A$, and $s\circ\mathcal F$ its underlying presheaf of sets. Then $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf with values in $\mathcal A$ (for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ the diagram $\mathcal F(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal F(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal F(U_i\times_UU_j)$ is an equalizer diagram in $\mathcal A$, Sites Definition 00VR and the discussion before it) if and only if $s\circ\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of sets (the same diagram of underlying sets is an equalizer diagram of sets).

source.place: Section 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), property ($\alpha$): a presheaf with values in a type of algebraic structure is a sheaf iff its underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf, referring to the proof of Sheaves Lemma sheaves-lemma-sheaves-structure (literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex); abelian groups and rings are types of algebraic structure by Sheaves Lemma sheaves-lemma-list-algebraic-structures
